assessments.reasoning: Authenticity follows from publisher_live's creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.txt URL. Integrity follows from the matching scoped full-file digest and cited [5884,6024) digest, with publisher_pin reporting the same full-file digest. Relevance follows from section 4(a) naming both classes of rights and their holder. Interpretation follows from its words “licensed or otherwise affected by this document” following the exclusions for waiver, abandonment and surrender. Applicability follows from the Statement of Purpose defining the Affirmer through application of CC0 to a Work. The contradiction check against sections 1(iv), 2, 3 and 4(c) confirms the express limitation survives both mechanisms and that other persons' rights require separate clearance analysis.

challenge.method: Read the broad purpose language, the unfair-competition provision, the waiver, the fallback license and its residual non-assertion language against sections 4(a) and 4(c).
challenge.results: Section 1(iv) expressly subjects unfair-competition rights to 4(a). Neither the breadth of permitted purposes in section 2 nor failure of the waiver in section 3 enlarges the rights reached. Section 3's residual undertaking likewise concerns remaining Copyright and Related Rights and associated claims. Section 4(c) addresses the distinct question of third-party clearance.

limitations: The conclusion concerns what this instrument does when the Affirmer applies it. Ownership, separate grants and available defenses in a particular case require separate evidence.
Section 4(c) disclaims responsibility for clearing other persons' rights or obtaining permissions. It supplies no finding about which third-party rights exist.
reasoning: Section 4(a) expressly covers trademark and patent rights “held by Affirmer”. Section 2 waives the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights to the extent permitted by law. Section 4(a) excludes the specified trademark and patent rights from waiver, abandonment and surrender. If the waiver is judged ineffective, section 3 licenses the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights to the affected extent. Section 4(a) separately excludes licensing or any other effect on the specified trademark and patent rights.
